# PEN-6275 — gate the Job pod ServiceAccount on an operator allowlist

[PEN-6275](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-6275).
Files: `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`,
`src/server/config-schema.ts`.

`resolveServiceAccountName()` is now gated on an operator-controlled allowlist,
`PAPERCLIP_ALLOWED_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAMES`, reusing the existing BLO-21812 throw
rather than inventing a second refusal disposition.

It previously took `config.serviceAccountName` **verbatim** — no allowlist, no
pattern, no validation — and this adapter sets `automountServiceAccountToken`
nowhere, so the pod inherits that setting from the ServiceAccount the config
NAMES: naming a sibling account in the namespace does not relabel the pod, it
mounts that account's RBAC at
`/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`.

## Why the gate is in the resolver and not at the config merge

**Three** scopes write the key and no single upstream point sees all of them:
the agent row, the issue-scope `assigneeAdapterOverrides.adapterConfig` overlay,
and `mergeEnvironmentConfig` (`execute.ts`), which copies an execution target's
config over the adapter config for every non-null key. PEN-6247 pinned the key
into the server's `AGENT_SCOPE_ONLY_CONFIG_KEYS`, closing the overlay only;
environment scope is not a theoretical third route but the production writer of
this key for the Penstock fleet (`onprem-k8s`'s
`paperclip/penstock-agent-environment-reconciler.yaml` writes
`config->>'serviceAccountName'` into environment rows).

## Two design decisions, pinned by tests rather than left to a reader

**Unset means NOT enforced.** Measured 2026-11-09: 39 live agent-job pods in ns
`paperclip` resolve to four different ServiceAccounts and 21 mount a token, so
refusing on an unset list would fail every dispatch on the deploy that carried
it. The gate's value is forcing the enumeration, not the refusal.

**The fleet default is NOT exempt**, even though it is set by the same operator
on the same Deployment. The Blockcast overlay sets
`PAPERCLIP_DEFAULT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAME: paperclip` — the control plane's own
ServiceAccount, `automountServiceAccountToken: true`, `Role/paperclip-k8s-adapters`
granting namespace-wide `secrets` and `batch/jobs` — and 16 of those 39 pods
reach it by the default with no per-agent value. Exempting the default would
exempt precisely the case the gate exists for.

Both arms are tested: a refused foreign SA and a permitted agent SA that still
renders. The must-pass arm is deliberate — a gate that only ever refuses is not
shown to work.

## Scope

This closes the `claude_k8s` half. The `opencode_k8s` sibling is vendored into
the same image and carries its own copy of the same gate; see
`vendor/paperclip-adapter-opencode-k8s/PROVENANCE-CHANGES.d/pen-6275.md`. The
two packages have no dependency edge, so the parser is copied rather than
imported and the pair has to be kept in step by hand.

Complements, and does not duplicate, `onprem-k8s`'s
`kyverno/policy-paperclip-serviceaccount-allowlist.yaml`, which covers every Pod
creator in the namespace but is `validationFailureAction: Audit` with its
Enforce flip held on PEN-2786.

No RBAC object is created or modified, and no behaviour changes until an
operator sets the env var.
